*Market data, adoption trends, and ROI metrics showing how low-code platforms are changing production application development*


The low-code development market has crossed a critical threshold. What was once considered a shortcut for simple prototypes now powers business applications across industries. The global market,[valued at $24.8 billion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) in 2023, is projected to reach $101.7 billion by 2030. For non-technical founders and business owners looking to capitalize on this shift,[Floot](https://floot.com/) provides a way to build and publish full-stack web applications without manually managing infrastructure.


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development according to its connector permissions, while Floot provides managed infrastructure such as hosting, Postgres databases, authentication, and storage.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Market growth is substantial** : The low-code application development platform market is projected to expand at a[22.5% CAGR](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) from 2024 to 2030, reaching $101.7 billion.
- **Enterprise adoption has accelerated** : Forrester reported that[87% of enterprise developers](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/category/low-code-platforms/) used low-code platforms for at least some development work in its research published in 2024.
- **Development speed can improve significantly** : Forrester noted that low-code platforms have the potential to make software development[up to 10 times faster](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/why-you-need-to-know-about-low-code-even-if-youre-not-responsible-for-software-delivery/) than traditional methods in suitable use cases.
- **Citizen development is expanding** : Gartner forecasts that[80% of low-code users](https://www.curoservices.com/getting-high-on-low-code/) would come from outside formal IT departments by 2026, illustrating the anticipated shift toward business-led application development.
- **Floot supports full-stack development** : Through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , Floot lets builders use supported AI assistants for application development while providing managed databases, authentication, storage, and hosting.


## **The Rise of Low-Code Development Platforms**


The software industry has fundamentally changed how applications get built. Traditional development, with its lengthy timelines and specialized skill requirements, often struggles to keep pace with business demands. Low-code platforms have emerged as a practical alternative for suitable applications.


### **1. Market valued at $24.8 billion in 2023**


The global low-code application development platform market reached[$24.8 billion in 2023](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) , establishing low-code as a significant segment of enterprise software. Grand View Research's historical estimate provides a baseline for measuring subsequent market expansion. The figure covers low-code application development platforms rather than every type of no-code or AI development tool. Understanding this distinction matters when comparing market forecasts from different research firms.


### **2. Projected to reach $101.7 billion by 2030**


Growth projections show the global market expanding to[$101.7 billion by 2030](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) , reflecting increasing demand for simplified application development. This Grand View Research forecast focuses on low-code application development platforms and uses 2023 as its historical market baseline. The projection suggests substantial long-term expansion, although the final market size will depend on adoption rates, technology changes, and enterprise software spending.


### **3. 22.5% compound annual growth rate**


Grand View Research projected a[22.5% CAGR](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) for the global low-code application development platform market from 2024 to 2030. This forecast reflects expectations of sustained demand for development platforms that simplify application delivery. The percentage represents projected compound annual market growth, not the growth rate achieved by every provider. Actual performance can vary across regions, industries, and individual platform categories.


### **4. $44.6 billion market size forecast for 2026**


Grand View Research estimated that the low-code application development platform market would reach[$44.6 billion in 2026](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) , compared with $24.8 billion in 2023. This figure is part of the research firm's broader market forecast through 2030. It represents an estimate rather than independently confirmed final 2026 revenue. The projected increase highlights expectations for broader enterprise adoption and continued investment in simplified software development.


### **5. $58.2 billion projected by 2029**


Gartner projected that the broader low-code development technologies market would reach[$58.2 billion by 2029](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/7146430) , with a forecast compound annual growth rate of 14.1%. Published in November 2025, the forecast identifies citizen development, agentic AI, and operational efficiency as important growth drivers. Gartner's market definition differs from Grand View Research's, so their market totals should not be treated as directly interchangeable estimates.


### **6. North America held 32.55% market share in 2023**


North America[accounted for 32.55%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) of the global market in 2023, according to Grand View Research. This regional share identifies North America as the largest market in the study's historical baseline. The region's enterprise software ecosystem and demand for application modernization support continued interest in low-code development. However, the percentage measures revenue share in 2023 rather than adoption among all North American businesses.


## **Democratizing App Development with Low-Code Tools**


Low-code platforms have opened software creation to people without traditional programming backgrounds. This shift addresses a fundamental problem: businesses need more applications than their professional development teams can always deliver.


### **7. 87% of enterprise developers use low-code**


Professional developers have embraced low-code tools, with[87% using them](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/category/low-code-platforms/) for at least part of their development work, according to Forrester research published in January 2024. This finding demonstrates that low-code is not exclusively intended for non-technical users. Experienced developers can also use these platforms to reduce repetitive implementation work, accelerate delivery, and focus their attention on more complex application requirements.


### **8. 80% of low-code users were forecast to come from outside IT by 2026**


Gartner forecast that[80% of low-code users](https://www.curoservices.com/getting-high-on-low-code/) would work outside traditional IT departments by 2026, up from 60% in 2021. This historical prediction illustrates the anticipated growth of citizen development. Employees with direct knowledge of business workflows can increasingly participate in application creation. The percentage remains a forecast and should not be interpreted as a verified final adoption rate for 2026.


### **9. 70% of new applications were projected to use low-code by 2025**


Gartner projected that[70% of new applications](https://www.informationweek.com/software-services/can-ai-lead-the-way-in-low-code-no-code-app-development-) developed by enterprises would use low-code or no-code technologies by 2025, compared with less than 25% in 2020. The forecast reflected expectations of rapid adoption across enterprise development teams. It did not establish that the projected percentage was ultimately achieved. The distinction matters when using historical forecasts to understand long-term software development trends.


### **10. 70% of low-code newcomers learned to build within one month**


A low-code adoption analysis reported that approximately[70% of inexperienced users](https://kpmg.com/sk/en/insights/2023/05/low-code-high-value-for-digital-transformation.html) learned to develop meaningful applications within one month. This finding suggests that simplified development environments can reduce the initial learning burden for people without previous platform experience. However, learning to create an application does not automatically establish production readiness. More complex applications still require testing, data management, security controls, and ongoing maintenance.


### **11. 80% of technology products were forecast to be built by non-IT professionals by 2024**


Gartner predicted that[80% of technology](https://www.index.dev/blog/no-code-low-code-statistics) products and services would be built by people outside traditional technology roles by 2024. This historical forecast anticipated a broader shift toward business-led technology creation, not just mobile app development. Its scope includes products and services beyond low-code applications. The forecast does not establish how many technology products were actually developed by non-IT professionals in 2024.


### **12. 75% of large enterprises were forecast to use four low-code platforms by 2025**


Gartner forecast that[75% of large enterprises](https://kpmg.com/sk/en/insights/2023/05/low-code-high-value-for-digital-transformation.html) would use at least four low-code development tools by 2025 for IT application development and citizen development initiatives. The prediction reflected expectations that enterprises would adopt multiple tools for different business needs. It should not be interpreted as evidence that every enterprise requires four platforms or that the forecasted adoption level was ultimately achieved.


For non-technical founders building MVPs, lower technical barriers can make application creation more accessible.[Floot's MCP integration](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) extends this approach by allowing supported AI assistants to create, edit, and publish applications through natural-language instructions. Available actions depend on the connected assistant's permissions and capabilities.


## **Accelerating Time-to-Market with Low-Code Development**


Speed has become a major driver of low-code adoption. Organizations facing competitive pressure often need to deliver applications and iterate on existing software without waiting through lengthy traditional development cycles.


### **13. Development can be up to 10 times faster**


Forrester noted that low-code platforms have the potential to make software development[up to 10 times faster](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/why-you-need-to-know-about-low-code-even-if-youre-not-responsible-for-software-delivery/) than traditional coding methods. The 2018 analysis highlighted reusable components, visual interfaces, and simplified development workflows as important advantages. This estimate describes potential acceleration in suitable projects rather than a guaranteed improvement. Development speed still depends on application complexity, testing requirements, integrations, and the experience of the development team.


### **14. Development time could be reduced by 50% to 90%**


Research commentary from 451 Research suggested that low-code platforms could reduce development time by[50% to 90%](https://www.informationweek.com/software-services/low-code-what-it-needs-to-know) compared with conventional programming approaches. The estimate was particularly relevant to simpler applications such as forms, surveys, registrations, and process-oriented mobile tools. It represents potential time savings, not a universal result across all software projects. Complex systems may require substantial custom development and integration work.


### **15. Organizations were reported to build software 56% faster**


An industry statistics roundup reported that organizations using low-code platforms developed software[56% faster](https://www.index.dev/blog/no-code-low-code-statistics) than those relying on traditional approaches alone. This comparison illustrates the reported potential for faster delivery through simplified development workflows. However, the roundup does not establish that every organization experiences the same improvement. Results depend on project scope, existing systems, application requirements, and the team's development practices.


### **16. 43.5% of developers reported saving up to 50% of project time**


A 2024 Reveal survey, summarized by New Horizons, found that[43.5% of developers](https://www.newhorizons.com/resources/blog/benefits-of-low-code) reported saving up to half their time on projects when using low-code tools. This result reflects the experiences of survey respondents rather than a measured productivity gain across the industry. Reduced time spent on repetitive development tasks may create more capacity for testing, feature improvements, and business-specific customization.


### **17. 90.4% reported productivity improvements**


In the same 2024 Reveal survey,[90.4% of respondents](https://www.newhorizons.com/resources/blog/benefits-of-low-code) said low-code tools had improved productivity in their organizations. The finding demonstrates strong positive sentiment among the surveyed developers. It measures reported productivity improvements rather than independently verified increases in software output. Teams evaluating low-code tools should still assess their own development times, application quality, and maintenance requirements before estimating potential returns.


## **The Role of Low-Code in Mobile App Development**


Mobile-first strategies require rapid application development across multiple platforms. Low-code tools have helped make cross-platform development more accessible, although mobile packaging and app store publication still involve platform-specific requirements.


### **18. 25% of low-code adopters reported very strong use for mobile app development**


According to KPMG's 2025 research,[25% of low-code users](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/sa/pdf/2025/accelerating-digital-transformation-with-ai-and-low-code.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf) reported very strong use of low-code platforms for mobile application development, while another 22% reported strong use. Adoption intensity varied by region, with 30% in the United States and 28% in Asia Pacific reporting very strong use, compared with 19% in Europe. Based on responses from 1,193 IT and business executives already using low-code, these findings highlight mobile development as an established use case for low-code platforms, although they do not measure market growth or future CAGR.


For teams building mobile applications,[Floot's mobile workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) support iOS and Android builds on every plan. Free includes 2 builds per month, Pro includes 12, and Power includes unlimited builds. Floot handles these builds without requiring local Xcode or Android Studio installations. Publishing requires the relevant developer account and app store approval, while connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan.


## **Low-Code vs. No-Code: Understanding the Nuances**


The distinction between low-code and no-code platforms often confuses buyers. Low-code typically reduces manual coding through visual or declarative tools, while no-code emphasizes workflows that require little or no programming.


### **19. Low-code was projected to account for over 65% of development activity by 2024**


Gartner previously forecast that low-code application development would represent[more than 65%](https://www.curoservices.com/getting-high-on-low-code/) of application development activity by 2024. This prediction reflected expectations that simplified development methods would become increasingly important in enterprise software delivery. However, the forecast does not establish the actual proportion reached in 2024. It also should not be interpreted as proof that traditional coding was expected to disappear.


Floot takes an AI-assisted full-stack approach, working alongside Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) . The connected AI assistant handles development according to its available permissions, while Floot provides managed databases, authentication, storage, and hosting for working applications.


## **Enhancing Business Process Automation with Low-Code**


Process automation remains an important use case for low-code platforms. Organizations struggling with manual workflows can use simplified development tools to digitize operations and reduce pressure on technical teams.


### **20. 88% of IT leaders reported increased workloads during the pandemic**


A 2021 survey reported that[88% of IT leaders](https://www.lowcodeplaza.com/industry-news/92-of-it-leaders-comfortable-with-business-users-using-low-code-tools/) experienced increased workloads during the preceding year. Among those reporting an increase, 60% said their workload had grown by more than half. These findings reflected the unusual pressure created by rapid digital transformation during the pandemic. They should not be treated as current workload measurements, but they illustrate why organizations began exploring faster development and automation methods.


### **21. Only 37% of organizations completed all requested IT projects**


A 2021 industry survey reported that only[37% of organizations](https://www.lowcodeplaza.com/industry-news/92-of-it-leaders-comfortable-with-business-users-using-low-code-tools/) said their IT teams had completed every project requested during the previous year. This finding illustrated a substantial delivery gap during a period of increased digital demand. The result is historical rather than a current project-completion rate. Low-code tools can help address some backlogs, but effective prioritization and sufficient resources remain important.


For small business owners needing custom internal tools,[Floot's built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) include managed Postgres databases, authentication, file storage, email, and scheduled jobs. These services reduce the amount of backend infrastructure that teams need to configure themselves.


## **Low-Code for Rapid Prototyping and MVP Development**


Startups and innovation teams use low-code platforms to validate ideas quickly before committing significant engineering resources. Reported savings can be substantial, but estimates should be interpreted within their original assumptions.


### **22. $4.4 million in modeled business value over three years**


An industry[estimate of $4.4 million](https://www.index.dev/blog/no-code-low-code-statistics) in business value over three years was associated with avoiding two additional developer hires through low-code or no-code development. The estimate describes a modeled business-value scenario, not a standard salary saving or guaranteed financial return. Actual outcomes depend on staffing costs, application complexity, productivity improvements, implementation expenses, and the value delivered by the resulting software.


### **23. No-code platforms may require 70% fewer resources**


An industry roundup reports that no-code platforms can use[70% fewer resources](https://www.index.dev/blog/no-code-low-code-statistics) than conventional application development approaches. The estimate suggests potential efficiency gains when projects can be delivered with simplified tools and reusable components. However, the source does not establish equivalent reductions in total expenditure or staffing needs for every organization. Resource requirements depend on application functionality, integrations, testing, security, and ongoing maintenance.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with 100 daily building actions and a $3 starter hosting allowance on the Free plan. Pro costs $25/month and includes 1,000 daily building actions and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. These options let founders test application ideas before moving to higher-capacity plans.


## **Low-Code Market Segments and Regional Growth**


Market research highlights differences in revenue contribution across low-code platform components and geographic regions. These figures help explain how the industry is structured and where future growth is expected.


### **24. Platform components held more than 71% market share in 2023**


Platform components accounted for[more than 71%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) of market revenue in 2023, according to Grand View Research. This indicates that the platform segment represented the majority of revenue within the studied low-code application development market. The statistic concerns market structure rather than the security performance of individual platforms. Organizations must still assess authentication, access controls, data protection, and operational requirements when choosing development infrastructure.


### **25. Asia Pacific forecast to grow at 25.0% CAGR**


Grand View Research projected a[25.0% CAGR](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/horizon/outlook/low-code-application-development-platform-market/asia-pacific) for the Asia Pacific low-code application development platform market from 2024 to 2030. This projection reflects expectations of substantial regional expansion, but it remains a forecast rather than a measured growth outcome. Actual growth will depend on enterprise adoption, investment conditions, and regional technology demand.


## **The Developer Talent Crisis Driving Low-Code Adoption**


Demand for software development expertise remains an important consideration for organizations. Low-code platforms can help some teams deliver applications with fewer specialized development resources, although they do not eliminate the need for technical oversight.


### **26. Global shortage of 4 million developers was forecast by 2025**


An older IDC forecast projected a global shortage of approximately[4 million developers](https://business.linkedin.com/learn/resources/learning-insights/closing-the-tech-talent-gap) by 2025. The prediction, also reported by LinkedIn Learning, reflected expectations of continued competition for software engineering talent. It does not establish the actual shortage recorded in 2025. Nevertheless, the historical forecast helps explain why organizations have explored low-code development, employee upskilling, and business-led application creation.


### **27. Average US software developer salary was $132,930 in 2022**


Hiring costs are substantial, with the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reporting a mean annual software developer[wage of $132,930](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2022/may/oes151252.htm) in May 2022. This figure represents the national occupational mean for that year, not a current salary estimate or the typical total cost of employment. Actual hiring expenses also depend on benefits, location, experience, recruitment costs, and the specific technical skills required.


### **28. Developers spent 13.5 hours weekly on technical debt in a 2018 study**


A 2018 Stripe study estimated that developers spent an average of[13.5 hours per week](https://lsvp.com/stories/the-developer-productivity-manifesto-part-3-leaving-software-on-the-table/) addressing technical debt. The finding illustrates how maintaining and correcting existing systems can consume development capacity. It reflects the respondents and working conditions studied in 2018 rather than a current industry average. Reducing technical debt requires appropriate engineering practices, maintenance, and software architecture decisions.


### **29. Developers spent 17.3 hours weekly on maintenance in a 2018 study**


The same Stripe research estimated that developers spent[17.3 hours per week](https://lsvp.com/stories/the-developer-productivity-manifesto-part-3-leaving-software-on-the-table/) on maintenance-related activities, including technical debt and fixing problematic code. The reported total included 13.5 hours of technical debt work and another 3.8 hours addressing bad code. These figures show the maintenance burden identified in the 2018 survey. They should not be treated as current measurements or as time that low-code tools automatically eliminate.


### **30. 26% of executives prioritized low-code automation investment**


Research reported by KPMG found that[26% of executives](https://www.cio.com/article/193919/the-road-to-modern-delivery-low-code-development-market-speed-and-the-future-of-it.html) identified low-code or no-code platforms as their most important automation investment during a 2020 survey period, compared with 10% in an earlier phase. The change reflected increased interest during the pandemic's initial digital transformation surge. It was a historical survey comparison rather than evidence of present-day investment priorities. The result illustrates how changing business conditions can influence automation decisions.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the primary benefit of using a low-code development platform?**


The primary benefit is often faster application development. Forrester estimated that low-code platforms could make development up to[10 times faster](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/why-you-need-to-know-about-low-code-even-if-youre-not-responsible-for-software-delivery/) in suitable use cases. This acceleration comes from simplified development workflows, reusable components, and reduced manual implementation. Results depend on project complexity, and speed improvements should not be interpreted as guaranteed financial savings.


### **Can low-code platforms be used to build production-grade applications?**


Yes, for suitable use cases. Production readiness depends on the application's security, reliability, testing, and operational requirements. Platforms like Floot provide[managed backend services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including Postgres databases, authentication, hosted assets, and application infrastructure. These capabilities can support production applications, although developers and app owners remain responsible for ensuring that their specific implementation meets applicable requirements.


### **What kind of businesses typically benefit most from low-code solutions?**


Organizations with limited development resources but significant software needs can benefit from low-code tools. Examples include non-technical founders building MVPs, small businesses creating internal systems, and teams automating repetitive workflows. Research also suggests that[87% of enterprise developers](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/category/low-code-platforms/) were already using low-code for some development work in a survey reported in 2024, showing relevance beyond non-technical users.


### **Is it possible to develop mobile applications using Floot?**


Yes. Floot supports[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) on Free (2 per month), Pro (12 per month), and Power (unlimited). Floot handles the builds without requiring users to install Xcode or Android Studio locally. Publishing requires the relevant Apple or Google developer account and store approval. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan.


### **What are the ownership guarantees for projects built on Floot?**


Floot states that users retain ownership of their application code, data, and intellectual property. Its[self-hosting documentation](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) explains how users can export project code and database backups. Full project ZIP downloads are available on paid plans, while database exports can be accessed separately. Self-hosting may require replacing services tied to Floot's managed infrastructure, including authentication, storage, email, or background jobs.
